Il carcinoma infiltrante di tipo non spe:
Invasive carcinoma of no special type (NST, formerly «invasive ductal») is the most common malignant tumour of the breast. The neoplastic cells form nests, cords or glands that infiltrate the stroma, often with a fibrous reaction. The histological grade (Nottingham) adds three scores: tubule formation, nuclear pleomorphism and mitoses. The biological subtype cannot be seen on haematoxylin-eosin: immunohistochemistry for oestrogen and progesterone receptors and for HER2 is needed. In this patient the tumour was triple negative (ER−, PR−, HER2−): a subtype that is often high grade, with solid growth and «pushing» margins, a lymphocytic infiltrate and sometimes central necrosis. Correlation with the MRI of the same patient (case 147): the irregular mass with rim enhancement and a non-enhancing centre corresponds to a solid tumour, cellular at the periphery, with a less vascularised centre.
